title: Season Enum
story: Your weather app shows different UI themes depending on the season. Spring gets pastel green, Summer gets bright yellow, Autumn gets warm orange, Winter gets cool blue. You need an enum that cycles through seasons and returns season-specific data like weather descriptions and months.
why: An enum with a `next` method that cycles through variants teaches state transitions using match.
analogy: Seasons are like a circular calendar. next is the arrow that moves the dial forward one quarter. weather reads the forecast for the current quarter. The cycle never ends — Winter wraps back to Spring, just like in real life.
try_it: Add a `Season.emoji(self) -> Str` method that returns a season-appropriate emoji. Add a `Season.average_temp(self) -> Int` method for each season. Add a `Season.activities(self) -> Str` method listing 2-3 activities per season.
tips: Methods can return enum values — `next` returns a `Season`, not a string
The `next` method is a state machine: each input maps to exactly one output
Chain `next()` calls: `s.next().next()` jumps two seasons ahead
common_mistakes: Forgetting the `Winter => Spring` mapping in `next` — without it, the cycle breaks in winter
Trying to set `s = Season.Winter` inside `next` instead of returning it — methods return values, they don't modify the receiver
